vulns.title: SQL injection in the catalogue search (fragment interpolated into SQL one layer down)
vulns.notes: router routers/catalogue.py:list_items passes the query value to repositories.catalogue_repo.search_items, which builds the statement with an f-string (cross-module). Route entry: routers/catalogue.py:23.

vulns.title: SQL injection in sign-in (JSON body handle concatenated into SQL)
vulns.notes: pydantic body field `handle` reaches repositories.account_repo.authenticate, which concatenates it into the statement. JSON body parameter, not a form field. Route entry: routers/accounts.py:26.

vulns.title: Reflected XSS in the catalogue lookup (term pasted into an HTMLResponse)
vulns.notes: the term is interpolated into markup returned as HTMLResponse, so the raw characters survive.

vulns.title: Template XSS: label rendered with |safe in detail.html
vulns.notes: TemplateResponse('detail.html', label=...) where the template renders {{ label|safe }} (templates/detail.html). Code location points at the Python render call, as in Mock A's M04.

vulns.title: Command injection in the diagnostics endpoint (os.system)
vulns.notes: routers/ops.py:diagnose calls services.net.probe_endpoint, which passes the value to os.system inside an f-string (cross-module). Route entry: routers/ops.py:25.

vulns.title: Command injection in the archive endpoint (subprocess shell=True)
vulns.notes: JSON body field `tag` reaches services.archive.snapshot, which runs a shell command string. Route entry: routers/ops.py:31.

vulns.title: Path traversal in the asset reader (os.path.join + open, no containment check)
vulns.notes: an absolute payload also works because os.path.join discards the base when the second part is absolute.

vulns.title: Path traversal in the raw asset route (path converter into FileResponse)
vulns.notes: the {name:path} converter keeps separators, so an encoded traversal reaches FileResponse.

vulns.title: Open redirect in the bounce endpoint (unvalidated RedirectResponse target)
vulns.notes: no allow-list; protocol-relative and absolute off-site targets are both honoured.

vulns.title: Open redirect after sign-in (post-authentication onward target)
vulns.notes: same route as B02 but a different parameter: the redirect is only reachable with valid credentials (avery / pepper-ridge).

vulns.title: Hard-coded session signing secret
vulns.notes: literal assigned to SIGNING_SECRET in config.py.

vulns.title: Hard-coded warehouse database password
vulns.notes: literal password, also embedded in the DSN string on the following line.

vulns.title: Hard-coded vendor pricing feed token
vulns.notes: literal token in the pricing service, used to build an Authorization header.

vulns.title: Missing security headers on every response (no CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy)
vulns.notes: host-wide: the app sets no security headers anywhere.

vulns.title: Session cookie set without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite
vulns.notes: set on the sign-in response; needs valid credentials (avery / pepper-ridge) to observe.

vulns.title: Verbose error page returns a full Python traceback
vulns.notes: the global exception handler renders traceback.format_exception to the client.

vulns.title: Server banner discloses the application version
vulns.notes: host-wide: a middleware stamps a versioned Server header on every response.

decoys.reason: parameterised query with a bound placeholder
value cast to int before use in SQL
os.path.basename plus a resolved-root containment check
redirect target checked against an allow-list
value reflected as JSON, not HTML
